title: How America's allies can preserve the West
gist: William D. James argues that against the consensus expectation of allied hedging, America's four core allies — Australia, Japan, Poland and the UK — are instead 'stewarding': binding tighter to Washington on nuclear, intelligence and equipment while simultaneously building a lateral web of bilateral treaties and defence-industrial partnerships that preserve the US-built order without US leadership. The concrete expressions are the UK-Poland Northolt Treaty, the GCAP sixth-generation fighter, and Poland becoming the European production hub for South Korean K2 tanks and Chunmoo artillery.

insights.claim: 'Stewarding' is the practice by which core US allies reinforce one another through lateral security agreements, defence-industrial partnerships and minilateral arrangements — preserving what American power built rather than hedging against it.
insights.speaker: William D. James
insights.so_what: A named framework for reading allied behaviour that predicts continued, not reduced, allied defence spending and continued US equipment purchases alongside intra-allied deals.
insights.quote: the practice by which core allies reinforce one another through lateral security agreements, defence-industrial partnerships and minilateral arrangements
insights.locator: We can call this emerging pattern of behaviour ‘stewarding’

insights.claim: The overwhelming scholarly consensus that most US allies and partners will hedge their bets does not hold for America's core allies in Europe and the Indo-Pacific, who are deepening links with each other while remaining aligned with Washington.
insights.speaker: William D. James
insights.so_what: The 'allies are decoupling from America' narrative is overstated for the countries that matter most — bearish for anyone positioning on transatlantic rupture.
insights.quote: The overwhelming consensus is that most allies and partners will hedge their bets.Interestingly, this is not the case for America’s core allies.
insights.locator: Mindful of the Trump administration’s unilateralism

insights.claim: Hedging, per Darren Lim and Zack Cooper, means sending signals designed to generate ambiguity about security commitments and eschewing clear-cut alignment with any great power — which is precisely what stewarding does not do.
insights.speaker: William D. James
insights.so_what: Gives an operational test for distinguishing genuine allied drift from cooperative burden-shifting: look for ambiguity signals, not for new bilateral treaties.
insights.quote: states hedge by sending signals designed to ‘generate ambiguity’ about their security commitments, ‘eschewing clear-cut alignment with any great power’
insights.locator: As foreign policy experts Darren Lim and Zack Cooper contend

insights.claim: Core allies are taking steps to ensure China and Russia cannot carve out spheres of influence while US leadership wavers, despite being critical of the Trump administration, because the alternatives to the US-led order are unpalatable.
insights.speaker: William D. James
insights.so_what: Allied criticism of Washington should not be read as a prelude to realignment toward Beijing or Moscow.
insights.locator: While these four are cognisant of the longstanding flaws

insights.claim: Scepticism about American staying power predates Trump, tracing back to European reactions to Obama's 2011 'pivot' to Asia and the Biden administration's unilateral Afghanistan withdrawal in 2021, but has intensified unquestionably on Trump's watch.
insights.speaker: William D. James
insights.so_what: European rearmament is a structural 15-year trend, not a Trump-cycle trade that unwinds after 2028.
insights.locator: The reassurance problem predates this president

insights.claim: The UK-Poland Northolt Treaty commits both parties to cooperation beyond their existing NATO mutual defence obligations, names Russia as the most significant long-term threat to Euro-Atlantic security, and commits to joint development of a next-generation missile system.
insights.speaker: William D. James
insights.so_what: A named joint UK-Poland missile programme is a concrete new European munitions development stream outside US supply chains.
insights.locator: Under the Northolt Treaty

insights.claim: The Northolt Treaty is the third major security pact the UK has signed with a European ally in under a year, following the July 2025 Northwood Declaration with France on nuclear cooperation and the Kensington Treaty with Germany.
insights.speaker: William D. James
insights.so_what: The pace of UK bilateral treaty-signing is itself the signal — three major pacts in twelve months indicates institutional urgency, not rhetoric.
insights.locator: The Northolt Treaty is the third major security pact

insights.claim: Britain and France, Europe's only nuclear-armed states, affirmed in the Northwood Declaration that there is 'no extreme threat to Europe that would not prompt a response by our two nations'.
insights.speaker: William D. James
insights.so_what: An explicit Anglo-French extended deterrence statement partially substitutes for US nuclear reassurance in Europe — a material change in the European security equation.
insights.quote: no extreme threat to Europe that would not prompt a response by our two nations
insights.locator: In July 2025, Britain and France

insights.claim: The UK concluded the Geelong Treaty with Australia in 2025 specifically to insulate the bilateral dimension of the trilateral AUKUS pact from potential shocks emanating from Washington.
insights.speaker: William D. James
insights.so_what: AUKUS submarine and technology programmes have been deliberately structured to survive a US withdrawal — reduces execution risk for UK and Australian defence primes.
insights.quote: insulating the bilateral dimension of the trilateral AUKUS defence pact from potential shocks emanating from Washington
insights.locator: The British government also concluded the Geelong Treaty

insights.claim: The 2023 Hiroshima Accord gave the UK and Japan reciprocal access to each other's military bases and included a consultation clause in the event of external aggression, with both governments declaring each other their most important partner in their respective regions.
insights.speaker: William D. James
insights.so_what: Europe-Indo-Pacific security linkage is now treaty-backed, meaning a Taiwan contingency would implicate European forces more directly than commonly assumed.
insights.locator: These initiatives follow the 2023 Hiroshima Accord

insights.claim: After Russia's 2022 invasion the UK pledged to defend Finland and Sweden if attacked, providing cover until they joined NATO in 2023 and 2024 respectively — an act of regional stewardship carried out without waiting for Washington to lead.
insights.speaker: William D. James
insights.so_what: A precedent showing European powers will underwrite security gaps unilaterally — relevant to how a Ukraine postwar guarantee might be constructed without US participation.
insights.locator: Following Russia’s full-scale invasion in 2022

insights.claim: The UK and Germany now head the Ukraine Defence Contact Group, having assumed responsibility from the United States for coordinating weapons deliveries and training to Kyiv.
insights.speaker: William D. James
insights.so_what: The procurement demand centre for Ukraine has shifted to European capitals — European defence contractors, not US ones, are the marginal beneficiaries of continued Ukraine aid.
insights.locator: Beyond diplomatic statements, stewarding is visible

insights.claim: London is positioning itself as a convening power in Europe, leading the 10-state Joint Expeditionary Force designed to improve interoperability outside NATO's formal command structures, and in April 2026 announced a 'Northern Navies initiative' under First Sea Lord Sir Gwyn Jenkins for a multinational maritime force defending Northwest Europe and the High North.
insights.speaker: William D. James
insights.so_what: A new multinational naval structure centred on the Royal Navy implies demand for surface escorts, ASW and Arctic-capable platforms in Northern Europe.
insights.quote: it should not be seen as separate to NATO [and, by extension, the United States], but rather complementary to it
insights.locator: In April 2026, First Sea Lord General Sir Gwyn Jenkins

insights.claim: The E3 dialogue of the UK, France and Germany has been expanded to include Italy and Poland on matters relating to Ukraine, and France and the UK have floated leading a postwar reassurance force there.
insights.speaker: William D. James
insights.so_what: Poland and Italy's inclusion widens the European decision-making core on Ukraine — watch this grouping rather than the EU for the shape of any settlement guarantee.
insights.locator: Together with Germany, they both form part of the E3 dialogue

insights.claim: The Global Combat Air Programme, a trilateral Italy-Japan-UK sixth-generation fighter effort, was framed from the outset around 'upholding the rules-based, free and open international order' while emphasising future interoperability with the United States.
insights.speaker: William D. James
insights.so_what: GCAP is the flagship non-US next-generation combat aircraft programme and is explicitly designed to be US-interoperable rather than US-competing — lowering the political risk to its export prospects.
insights.quote: upholding the rules-based, free and open international order
insights.locator: The Global Combat Air Programme (GCAP)

insights.claim: GCAP was one of the few beneficiaries of the Labour government's recent Defence Investment Plan, illustrating cross-party support for the programme in the UK.
insights.speaker: William D. James
insights.so_what: Political durability across UK governments makes GCAP one of the safer long-duration defence programme exposures despite Treasury austerity elsewhere.
insights.locator: It is notable that GCAP was one of the few beneficiaries

insights.claim: Poland is acquiring nearly 300 Chunmoo artillery systems and up to 1,000 K2 Black Panther tanks from South Korea, with significant technology transfer that will make Poland the European hub for K2 and Chunmoo production.
insights.speaker: William D. James
insights.so_what: Poland becoming a European production hub for Korean systems creates a durable non-US, non-Western-European armour and rocket-artillery supply chain — a competitive threat to German and French land systems primes.
insights.quote: Poland is set to become the European hub for K2 and Chunmoo production
insights.locator: Warsaw is acquiring nearly 300 Chunmoo artillery systems

insights.claim: Poland and South Korea both recognise the linkage between European and Indo-Pacific security, underscored by the presence of North Korean soldiers in neighbouring Ukraine.
insights.speaker: William D. James
insights.so_what: North Korean troop deployments in Europe are the concrete mechanism converting two regional theatres into one — expect further cross-theatre defence-industrial deals.
insights.quote: the presence of North Korean soldiers in neighbouring Ukraine
insights.locator: Both states recognise the security relations between Europe

insights.claim: Poland has struck notable defence agreements with France and Germany within the past two years, alongside strategic partnerships with Canada and Sweden.
insights.speaker: William D. James
insights.so_what: Poland is diversifying suppliers and partners aggressively — a broad opportunity set for European defence exporters into the largest-growing NATO budget.
insights.locator: Poland, for its part, has struck notable agreements

insights.claim: Rather than decoupling, all four core allies are spending more on defence with American equipment earmarked for much of the new funding — Poland is acquiring F-35 fighters, HIMARS missile systems and Abrams tanks.
insights.speaker: William D. James
insights.so_what: US defence exporters remain primary beneficiaries of allied rearmament despite the political friction — the decoupling narrative is not showing up in procurement.
insights.quote: All four are spending more on defence, with American equipment earmarked for much of this new funding.
insights.locator: If anything, they are doubling down on the US

insights.claim: The UK is purchasing F-35As specifically to participate in NATO's nuclear-sharing mission using US B61 bombs, deepening its reliance on Washington for the reconstituted second arm of its nuclear deterrent.
insights.speaker: William D. James
insights.so_what: Britain is voluntarily increasing, not reducing, its nuclear dependence on the US — evidence against any near-term European nuclear autonomy thesis.
insights.locator: The UK, meanwhile, is purchasing F-35As

insights.claim: The 'crown jewels' of the Anglo-American alliance — institutional intelligence-sharing and nuclear relationships — endure at the deep bureaucratic level despite surface tensions between political leaders.
insights.speaker: William D. James
insights.so_what: Political noise between Downing Street and the White House is a poor indicator of the underlying alliance — do not trade headlines about transatlantic rifts.
insights.quote: the institutional intelligence-sharing and nuclear relationships – endure at the deep, bureaucratic level, despite occasional tensions at the surface between political masters
insights.locator: The ‘crown jewels’ of the Anglo-American alliance

insights.claim: AUKUS, involving transfer of sensitive nuclear propulsion technology, continues at 'full steam' according to Trump, with pillar-two collaboration across emerging technologies making recent progress in undersea warfare.
insights.speaker: William D. James
insights.so_what: AUKUS execution risk is lower than headlines imply; undersea warfare technology is the pillar-two area showing actual progress.
insights.locator: The AUKUS defence pact, which involves the transfer

insights.claim: Core allies are combining two approaches simultaneously — binding tighter to Washington while building lateral cooperation with one another to uphold deterrence in key regions — which is what distinguishes them from allies who are genuinely hedging.
insights.speaker: William D. James
insights.so_what: The dual strategy means defence budget growth accrues to both US and allied national primes — not a zero-sum reallocation.
insights.quote: These core allies, then, are combining two approaches: binding tighter to Washington, while building lateral co-operation with one another to uphold deterrence in key regions.
insights.locator: Such behaviour is what separates Australia, Japan, Poland

insights.claim: The Iran War exposed the parlous state of the British armed forces, with only one destroyer able to deploy to the region and belatedly at that.
insights.speaker: William D. James
insights.so_what: A single deployable destroyer is a hard capability ceiling that undercuts UK ambitions to lead new naval initiatives — expect pressure for accelerated shipbuilding orders.
insights.quote: with only one destroyer able to deploy to the region – and belatedly at that
insights.locator: The Iran War exposed the parlous state

insights.claim: Wrangling between the UK Treasury and the Ministry of Defence over the Defence Investment Plan underscores continued reluctance to return military spending to Cold War levels despite Europe's deteriorating security environment.
insights.speaker: William D. James
insights.so_what: UK defence budget growth will likely disappoint versus rhetoric — favour Polish and continental exposure over UK-domestic-demand defence names.
insights.locator: The wrangling between the UK Treasury

insights.claim: Poland is investing nearly five per cent of GDP in defence but starts from a lower base and has a long way to go before turning złoty into hard capabilities.
insights.speaker: William D. James
insights.so_what: Poland's ~5% of GDP is the highest allied commitment but with a long lag from budget to capability — sustained multi-year procurement flows rather than immediate deterrent value.
insights.quote: Poland, by contrast, is investing nearly five per cent of GDP in defence, though it starts from a lower base and has a long way to go before turning złoty into hard capabilities
insights.locator: Poland, by contrast, is investing nearly five per cent

insights.claim: Stewarding's prospects depend on allied cohesion and sustained investment, both of which are vulnerable to the whims of domestic politics, so expectations need to be managed even though the logic is sound.
insights.speaker: William D. James
insights.so_what: The key fragility in the European rearmament trade is domestic fiscal politics, not strategic intent — track budget votes rather than communiqués.
insights.quote: its prospects depend on allied cohesion and sustained investment, both of which are vulnerable to the whims of domestic politics
insights.locator: There is, however, a potential weak spot in stewarding

insights.claim: The May 2026 cancellation of a planned deployment of 4,000 US troops to Poland shocked Warsaw, and the administration only announced 5,000 soldiers would be sent instead following the backlash.
insights.speaker: William D. James
insights.so_what: US force posture in Eastern Europe is now reversible on short notice and responsive to political backlash — a volatility source for regional risk assets.
insights.locator: The unexpected cancellation in May 2026

insights.claim: For British strategists the gravest concerns are not tariffs or basing disputes but Trump's threats to annex Greenland and his apparent endorsement of Russia's territorial claims in Ukraine, both of which imply acceptance that 'might makes right'.
insights.speaker: William D. James
insights.so_what: The allied trust rupture is about territorial norms, not trade — meaning tariff resolutions will not repair the strategic relationship.
insights.quote: Both mark an implicit acceptance that ‘might makes right’, a notion fundamentally at odds with the traditional principles of the US-led (and, by extension, British) world order.
insights.locator: The disputes over tariffs and basing are troubling

insights.claim: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney's view that the US-led order is already sinking with allies jumping ship is contradicted by the behaviour of America's core allies, who are reinforcing the vessel rather than scrambling for lifeboats.
insights.speaker: William D. James
insights.so_what: Directly rebuts a prominent G7 leader's framing — the base case should be alliance persistence with redistributed burden, not order collapse.
insights.quote: Yet America’s core allies are not scrambling for lifeboats.
insights.locator: If Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney is to be believed
